title: Mulholland Drive
events_chronological: Diane Selwyn wins a jitterbug contest in Deep River, Ontario, and comes to Hollywood on her dead aunt's money.
Diane meets the actress Camilla Rhodes on the set of The Sylvia North Story, loses the lead to her, and becomes her lover.
Camilla gets Diane bit parts out of pity while her own career takes off.
Camilla ends the affair, and Diane keeps calling her.
Camilla drives Diane up Mulholland Drive to a party at the director Adam Kesher's house.
At the party Camilla kisses another actress and she and Adam announce their engagement while Diane sits humiliated at the table.
In a diner Diane pays a hitman to kill Camilla, and he tells her she will find a blue key when it is done.
Diane wakes on her sofa, finds the blue key on the table, and begins to come apart.
In her dream Diane recasts herself as the fresh-faced Betty Elms, arriving in Los Angeles to stay in her aunt's flat.
A woman survives a staged crash on Mulholland Drive, walks down into the city with no memory, and hides in that same flat, calling herself Rita after a poster.
Betty and Rita find a handbag stuffed with cash and a blue key, and set out to discover who Rita is.
A hitman's simple killing goes farcically wrong across three bodies.
Director Adam Kesher is forced by the mob and by a figure called the Cowboy to cast an unknown blonde named Camilla Rhodes in his film.
A man at Winkie's describes a nightmare about a figure behind the diner and drops dead of fright when he sees it.
Betty auditions brilliantly and is taken to Adam's set, where their eyes meet across the sound stage.
Betty and Rita find a rotting corpse in Diane Selwyn's apartment and flee.
Betty and Rita become lovers, and Rita takes them at two in the morning to a theatre called Club Silencio where everything turns out to be a recording.
Betty finds a blue box in her handbag, Rita opens it with the blue key, and both women vanish out of the dream.
Awake and ruined, Diane hallucinates her miniature parents shrieking at her heels and shoots herself on her bed.
The Cowboy looks in at the door, the old couple crawl under it, and a woman in the balcony of Club Silencio says "Silencio".
syuzhet_notes: The film's first two-thirds - told-order bullets 2-11 - are a dream, and the audience is never told so at the time; the last third, bullets 12-18, is the waking life the dream was assembled from, delivered as a rush of fragments rather than a straight account. Told-order bullet 1 is a memory image with no fixed place in either, and the film shows the fantasy in full before showing anything it was made out of.
fabula_notes: The dream reading is the standard one but not the only one available; the film never states which parts are real, so this chronology is an interpretation rather than a transcription. Where the dream itself belongs in real time is also uncertain - it is placed here as a single night's sleep between Diane commissioning the murder and killing herself. Camilla's death is never shown.
